summary:
M1 (high) is fixed. Account erasure now takes LOCK TABLE legal_hold and refuses with 409 legal_hold before any credential invalidation or deletion when a hold covers the person, their organisation or an erased workspace. An integration test drives the real better-auth delete-user route, and each refusal is paired with a lifted-hold success.
M2, M3, M4, M6, M7, M8 and M9 are fixed in source with tests. M5 is fixed on paper: PA-1a now matches the allow-list and is recorded as accepted by Thomas on 23 Oct. That acceptance comes from the coordinator; I did not see it.
No critical or high finding remains. The new findings are one medium (process) and six lows: an unlisted presign route in the idempotency denylist, legacy task_comment cascade on erasure, weak coveredBy evidence in the auth-route inventory, a deep-link double confirm, PA-5 wording, and a held erasure that takes the identity-table lock before refusing. The registered deletion targets (column, label, canned response, invitation, relation, comment, attachment, work item) delete nothing held: work items, comments and attachments are soft-deleted, and a column delete sets task.column_id to null.
The one condition: AGENTS.md:20 requires browser verification on persisted data, and none was done (SIT Postgres down). P0 is implemented and AI-reviewed, but 'locally verified' cannot be claimed until the listed flows are checked in a browser.
The partial or blocked items (EV-1, EV-3, PA-4 origin, PA-5a, PA-13, PA-14) are carried with named phases. None of them is a P0 blocker under the stated bias.

round3_status.evidence: apps/api/src/user/controllers/delete-account-data.ts:165-194 refuseIfUnderLegalHold. It runs lockLegalHolds (utils/workspace-legal-hold.ts:27-29), then checks a person hold or organisation hold on the erasing user's persons, then isWorkspaceUnderOpenLegalHold for each plan.workspaceIdsToDelete. It throws APIError CONFLICT code legal_hold and is called at :310, before invalidateAccountDeletionCredentials (:312) and deleteWorkspaceRoleDependents (:321). The path is wired through auth.ts:382-387 (beforeDelete) and covers deleteUserCallback via the same hook. Test: tests/api-integration/account-erasure-legal-hold.test.ts:122-199 goes through POST /api/auth/delete-user. It covers a held stakeholder, a held erasing person and a held organisation, and asserts that the user, the workspace and the sessions survive, then that the erasure succeeds after the hold is lifted.

apps/web/src/components/shared/modals/create-task-modal.tsx:238-242 uses the store project only when project.id === resolvedProjectId, falling back to the workspaceProjects lookup. The upload key is built at :429-441. Test: create-task-modal.test.tsx:321-335 ('uploads to the created task's own project even when the store holds another project').

docs/technical/safety-and-runtime.md:2469-2486. tests/api-integration/delete-routes-never-immediate.test.ts:18-24,74-150,328-400. The test enumerates every live auth.api endpoint whose path matches delete, remove, revoke, unlink, disable or sign-out. Each must appear in AUTH_DESTRUCTIVE_ROUTES with a reason and a coveredBy file, with no stale entries. An anonymous probe asserts that user, session, key and workspace counts are unchanged and that /admin/* returns 404. The PATCH /api/task/bulk delete runtime test that asserts 410 and that the row survives is at task-target-reach.test.ts:541-564. Weaknesses are listed as K4.

apps/api/src/middleware/idempotency.ts:28-40 and :240-277. Every 2xx application/json response up to 256 KiB is stored and replayed, except the SECRET_BEARING_ROUTES denylist (step-up, SCIM rotate/revoke-token, metrics-token rotate, /api/auth, /api/me api-key/mfa/totp/backup, attachments/presign, invitations). The middleware is mounted for every non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS method at index.ts:1421-1424. Gap: PUT /api/task/image-upload/{id} (presigned URL) is not on the denylist (K2).

findings.requirement: AGENTS.md:20 (verify affected screens in a real browser on persisted data); PA-3
findings.problem: No browser verification was done in this round or earlier ones. The SIT Postgres was shut down at 00:44. Every PA-3 and UI claim (in-place approval dialog for each target, leaving the deleted task page on the legacy and canonical routes, create-task staged uploads to the right key, relation, saved-view and calendar dialogs, and member/role/workspace/project delete flows) rests on unit tests that mock react-query and the router.
findings.impact: The 'locally verified' state cannot be claimed for P0. The Kaneo-parity rule ('compare each touched screen against the Kaneo original in a browser') is unmet for the touched screens.
findings.recommended_fix: Before P0 is marked locally verified, restart a non-live test database (not taskdesk_browser_journey_1022_test with resetting fixtures) and walk these flows in a browser. Delete a task from its own page (legacy and /agent/work-items) and approve. Bulk delete. Comment and attachment delete. Relation remove. Saved-view delete. Service-calendar delete. Project, workspace and role delete with step-up. Create a task with staged files after first visiting another project's settings. Account deletion under a hold should show the 409 message. Record screenshots as phase evidence.

findings.requirement: PA-15 / api-design idempotency (secret-bearing responses are never persisted)
findings.problem: The denylist excludes /attachments/presign but not the legacy Kaneo image-upload route. That route answers 200 JSON carrying a presigned S3 PUT URL (or a filesystem-upload capability URL). A keyed PUT stores that URL in idempotency_key.response_body for 24 h, and a keyed retry replays it after it may have expired.
findings.impact: A short-lived upload credential is persisted in the database for 24 h, and a client retrying within 24 h gets a possibly expired URL and a failed upload. It is per-actor scoped and single-object, so exposure is low.
findings.recommended_fix: Add /\/image-upload\/[^/]+$/ (or a generic presign/upload-URL marker) to SECRET_BEARING_ROUTES and add it to the it.each case list in idempotency.test.ts. Better: let routes declare the flag next to their schema, so a new presign route cannot be missed.

findings.problem: For workspaces the erasing user leaves rather than deletes, the better-auth user-row delete cascades the legacy Kaneo task_comment rows they authored. The hold check covers the erasing person, their organisation and the erased workspaces. It does not cover a hold on a surviving workspace's or project's organisation, and authored content is meant to be retained regardless. time_entry and task_activity are SET NULL, so they survive.
findings.impact: Legacy imported Kaneo comments by the erasing user disappear from surviving, possibly held, workspaces. No current controller writes task_comment, so only imported legacy data is affected.
findings.recommended_fix: Change task_comment.user_id to ON DELETE SET NULL (nullable) in a migration, or have the erasure refuse when it would cascade task_comment rows under an open hold. Track this with the P1 legacy-data unification.

findings.problem: coveredBy is checked only for file existence. /unlink-account and /two-factor/disable name pending-action-credential-revocation.test.ts, which never calls either route (grep finds zero matches). The anonymous probe compares row counts, which proves nothing if those tables are empty when the probe runs, and it asserts status only for /admin/*.
findings.impact: The inventory forces classification of new better-auth routes, which is good. Its 'covered by' evidence overstates what is tested for two entries.
findings.recommended_fix: Point those entries at a test that exercises them, or mark them 'no business data; no dedicated test'. Seed one user, session, key and workspace before the anonymous probe, and assert a 401/403/404 status for every non-sign-out entry.

findings.requirement: PA-3 ('to the person it is a confirm dialog')
findings.problem: The ?action=delete deep-link entries for canned responses and labels show their own AlertDialog first and then the approval dialog, so the person confirms twice. The comment says this is deliberate, so a link cannot fire a request on its own.
findings.impact: Minor inconsistency with the row buttons, which confirm once. It is not a safety problem.
findings.recommended_fix: Either accept and document this as the deep-link pattern, or make the deep link open a neutral 'Request deletion' entry that goes straight to the approval dialog.

findings.file: docs/technical/safety-and-runtime.md:2469-2486 (PA-1a) and the PA-5 bullet that follows PA-4; apps/api/src/auth.ts:525-532
findings.problem: PA-5 still lists 'API key' deletion as elevated, while PA-1a exempts better-auth own-key revocation as immediate. In practice the route is session-only (enableSessionForAPIKeys: false, so an API key cannot call /api/auth/api-key/delete), but it has no typed confirmation and no pending action.
findings.impact: The two contract bullets contradict each other on the same route.
findings.recommended_fix: Amend PA-5 to say 'API-key creation/rotation' (or note the PA-1a revocation exemption) so the contract matches the code.

findings.requirement: PA-12 (M1 fix); availability of identity provisioning
findings.problem: The new legal-hold refusal runs only at :310. That is after the instance-wide LOCK TABLE person, membership_grant, membership IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE at :289-303, so a held user's refused erasure still takes that lock and evaluates the full workspaceUnderOpenHold union before it rolls back. The file's own rule at :246-249 says a refused erasure must not take the lock, because repeated refused calls could stall every provisioning writer (OIDC JIT login, SCIM).
findings.impact: A user under a hold, for example a departing employee, can repeat delete-user (password only) and repeatedly block person, grant and membership writers for the duration of the hold query. The data is never at risk; this is an availability nuisance only.
findings.recommended_fix: Run a cheap pre-lock pass of refuseIfUnderLegalHold (without lockLegalHolds) next to the first refuseIfOthersHaveAccess at :264, and keep the locked re-check at :310. Alternatively take lockLegalHolds before the table lock: legal_hold SHARE is compatible with the purge and workspace-delete holders, so no lock cycle is introduced.
